title: A uniform influence bound for hypergraph properties
main_claim: For every fixed r>=3, every vertex-permutation-invariant Boolean property f of r-uniform hypergraphs on n vertices satisfies Var_p(f) <= C_r I_p(f)/(log n)^{r/(r-1)} uniformly in 0<p<1, with no monotonicity assumption. For increasing properties this gives threshold width O_{r,eps}((log n)^{-r/(r-1)}), which the paper presents as the Friedgut–Kalai hypergraph conjecture.
coverage:
Read all of the LaTeX: introduction, fourier, restriction, completion. Checked each step by hand.
(1) Single-coordinate 4th-moment bound with rho=sigma/4. The coefficients 13sigma^2/32 and 9sigma^2/256 are correct, and so are the moment bounds |E chi^3| <= 1/sigma and E chi^4 <= 1/sigma^2. The induction to the product space works, as does the projection bound ||P_{<=k} g||_2 <= rho^{-k}||g||_{4/3}.
(2) The bound rho^{-2k} <= m^{1/16}, using sigma*log(4/sigma) <= 2. The case split on I(h) <= m^{1/4} gives m^{-5/16}. The identity ||Delta_i h||_{4/3}^2 = I_i^{3/2} holds.
(3) Parseval with derivatives: sum |S| f^(S)^2 = sigma^2 I.
(4) Restriction lemma: Sym(B) fixes the assigned coordinates. Orbits have size binom(m,j) >= m because 1 <= j <= r < m, so the hypothesis of Lemma 2.1 holds. E_y of the squared restricted coefficients is the right sum, E_y I_e(f_y) = I_e(f), and Pr(e in F_B) <= rm/n.
(5) Capture lemma: s <= v^r gives average degree rs/v <= r s^{(r-1)/r} <= k when s <= L = (k/r)^alpha, so some vertex has degree between 1 and k. Pr(B∩V={u}) >= (m/n)(1-(v-1)(m-1)/(n-1)) >= m/(2n) with v <= rL. The k in this lemma is the same k as in the restriction lemma.
(6) Completion: the four conditions defining N_r imply the capture condition, since k/r <= log n and (m-1)/(n-1) <= n^{-1/2}. The tail sigma^2/L = (64r)^alpha sigma^{2-alpha}/(log m)^alpha is at most (192r)^alpha/(log n)^alpha because alpha < 2 when r >= 3. The small-n constant is handled correctly.
(7) Corollary: Russo's formula, q(0)=0 and q(1)=1, strict monotonicity, and integration of the log-odds give the factor 2 log((1-eps)/eps).
sibling_notes: This paper shares its Fourier lemma and restriction method with the graph companion paper at rank 510, which the sibling branch also reported as no_gap_found. The only new ingredient is the min-degree capture bound for hypergraphs, and it checks out. The paper reproduces the companion's arguments in full rather than citing them, so it does not depend circularly on the companion. Caveat: this argument is short and claims to settle a known conjecture, so an independent expert should still check it. I found no step that fails.
